The transport of polyunsatured fatty acids (PUFA), such as aracidonic acid (ARA) and docosohexaenoic acide (DHA) to the fetus from the maternal stores increases depending of the fetal requirements for the PUFA during the final trimester of pregnancy, therefore, the maternal blood PUFA level changes physiologically during pregnancy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the present results may be used to evaluate the PUFA status of pregnant women and infants in the Japanese population.
the maternal erythrocyte ARA level at 27 weeks and the DHA level at 30 weeks of pregnancy are useful indicators for predicting the corresponding fatty acid level in cord blood.
the maternal blood PUFA levels in the last trimester may be used to estimate fetal PUFA levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the levels of PUFA in erythrocytes of pregnant women who habitually ate fish decreased with the progress of their pregnancy and increased again after childbirth.
the PUFA levels of the maternal blood after the third trimester may be used as a reliable marker to predict the levels of PUFA in the circulating blood of infants.
the fatty acids in maternal erythroycytes may be used as a marker of fetal nutrition.
